taskTitle: Twelve HTTP status codes, by the book

checks.detail: 3 subtasks, read from the schema reply
5 phases had the tools designed for them

finalText:
All 12 codes are defined in RFC 9110 (HTTP Semantics), which replaces RFC 7231. Three workers checked the codes against https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html. Their reports agree with each other, and each code's own section agrees with the summary list in Section 15.1. They did not compare against the httpwg.org copy. I had no tools myself, so this answer relies entirely on their reports.

**Which codes are heuristically cacheable**

Section 15.1 settles this. It says: "Responses with status codes that are defined as heuristically cacheable (e.g., 200, 203, 204, 206, 300, 301, 308, 404, 405, 410, 414, and 501 in this specification) can be reused by a cache with heuristic expiration unless otherwise indicated by the method definition or explicit cache controls [CACHING]; all other status codes are not heuristically cacheable." (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html)

- **Heuristically cacheable:** 203, 206, 308, 405, 410, 414 and 501. Each one's own section also says so, e.g. "A 308 response is heuristically cacheable; …" (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html)
- **Not heuristically cacheable:** 303, 307, 413, 421 and 422. None is in the list, and their own sections say nothing about it.

**Reason phrases RFC 9110 changed**

- 413 is now "Content Too Large"; older specs called it "Payload Too Large".
- 422 is now "Unprocessable Content"; RFC 4918 called it "Unprocessable Entity".
- 421 (from RFC 7540) and 422 are now defined in RFC 9110 itself.

**Summary by code**

| Code | Reason phrase | Section | Heuristically cacheable |
|---|---|---|---|
| 203 | Non-Authoritative Information | 15.3.4 | yes |
| 206 | Partial Content | 15.3.7 | yes |
| 303 | See Other | 15.4.4 | no |
| 307 | Temporary Redirect | 15.4.8 | no |
| 308 | Permanent Redirect | 15.4.9 | yes |
| 405 | Method Not Allowed | 15.5.6 | yes |
| 410 | Gone | 15.5.11 | yes |
| 413 | Content Too Large | 15.5.14 | no |
| 414 | URI Too Long | 15.5.15 | yes |
| 421 | Misdirected Request | 15.5.20 | no |
| 422 | Unprocessable Content | 15.5.21 | no |
| 501 | Not Implemented | 15.6.2 | yes |

Each quote in the JSON below comes from that code's own numbered section, as the workers read it with fetch_page.

{"code":"206","reason":"Partial Content","section":"15.3.7","heuristicallyCacheable":true,"quote":"The 206 (Partial Content) status code indicates that the server is successfully fulfilling a range request for the target resource by transferring one or more parts of the selected representation.","url":"https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html"},
{"code":"303","reason":"See Other","section":"15.4.4","heuristicallyCacheable":false,"quote":"This status code is applicable to any HTTP method.","url":"https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html"},

{"code":"308","reason":"Permanent Redirect","section":"15.4.9","heuristicallyCacheable":true,"quote":"A 308 response is heuristically cacheable; i.e., unless otherwise indicated by the method definition or explicit cache controls (see Section 4.2.2 of [CACHING]).","url":"https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html"},
